- Wizard step 5 (Oversized files): "Skip HDR files" now sits to the right of "Preferred GPU" in a two-column flex row instead of stacked below the description. Both controls align to the same height.
- Wizard step 8 (Language cleanup): the mdChipInput language pickers no longer sit taller than the emby-select controls next to them. Same 46px height rule that already applied on the Settings tab now applies inside the wizard too.
- Wizard step 2 (Libraries): the "Check library access" button now uses the plugin's mdActionBtn class (rounded pill, primary accent, 44px tall) instead of Jellyfin's raw raised-button styling. Matches the rest of the plugin.
- Wizard step 16 (Community stats): intro copy no longer starts with "Off by default -" and now lists every scanner in the "What's sent" panel.

Reclaim totals now match across the plugin, heavy-transcode fixer works on well-encoded sources, SMART shows correctly on unprivileged Linux, and the History tab lets you slice failures by reason.

Features
- History tab's Failed filter now surfaces a "search by reason" dropdown listing the distinct failure reasons in your history with a count each (Permission denied, I/O error, Cross-device link, File no longer exists, etc.). Selecting one narrows the list; switching the top-level chip clears it.
- SMART pill on the Overview drives now shows a specific hint when smartctl fails due to permissions on Linux: setcap 'cap_sys_rawio+ep' $(which smartctl) for native installs, --cap-add=SYS_RAWIO --device=... for Docker.

Bug fixes
- Overview "Reclaimed since install" and History tab's summary + per-library chart now show the same number. History was summing the paginated 500-row window client-side while Overview summed the entire history server-side, causing the mismatch (e.g. 599 GB vs 8.1 GB). New /History/Stats endpoint aggregates over all history server-side; both panels source the total from it.
- Heavy-transcode / failed-transcode fixes no longer refuse to swap when the re-encoded file is slightly larger than the original. Those fix types exist for direct-play compatibility, not disk savings â€” the size gate is now Quality-only, with a 30% hard cap on the transcode types to guard against misconfigured encode settings.
- SMART pills now appear on library drives on Linux. Library-drive detection was using Path.GetPathRoot which always returns "/" on Linux â€” no library drive was ever flagged, so the SMART probe never ran there. Now uses the deepest-matching mount point via FindDriveForPath.
- smartctl exit_status is now honoured. Non-zero exit (permission denied, unsupported device, no SMART support) returns Unknown with the actual smartctl error message, instead of being mis-interpreted as "self-assessment FAILED".

Bug fixes
- RecycleBin cross-volume moves verify copy size before deleting the source (no more silent data loss on truncated writes).
- MoveToBin folder names carry a per-batch GUID so same-millisecond recycles no longer collide.
- FileBrowser rename / move now return 409 on concurrent-target creation instead of silently overwriting.
- Upload endpoint rejects oversized bodies via Content-Length pre-flight before any disk I/O; 50 GB per-file cap.
- LibraryGuard refuses paths whose ancestor chain contains a symlink or NTFS junction.
- RecycleBinPath must sit inside the plugin data dir or a configured library; OS-reserved roots refused.
- SweepOrphanSidecars enumerates with reparse-point skip and re-checks each candidate before delete.
- IsSimpleName refuses Windows reserved names (CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9) and trailing dot / space.
- RelocateIssuePaths uses COLLATE NOCASE on the boundary match so sibling issues re-point correctly after case-varying moves on Windows.
- PlayabilityFixer re-verify is reason-driven (audio-kind files no longer recycled on "no-audio" false positives; size-truncated files now actually removed).
- TrackFixer.IsSelfReferentialSubtitle normalises both paths via Path.GetFullPath so legacy relative-path issue rows can't trick the guard.
- MediaSorterFixer cross-volume detection works on Linux (was previously blind because Path.GetPathRoot returns "/").
- MissingSubtitleFixer catches TaskCanceledException from provider network stalls without aborting the whole fix run.
- smartctl / nvidia-smi / df invocations use ArgumentList (no shell tokenization); absolute-path resolution on Linux where possible.
- WMI drive-letter validated before WQL interpolation.
- BulkUpdateOpenIssueStatus chunks at 500 params; controller caps requests at 50 k IDs.
- SmartHealthProbe stdout and stderr drained concurrently before WaitForExit (no more pipe-buffer deadlocks on large SMART payloads).
- Diagnostics ring buffer dedup keys off a hash of the pre-truncation message; entries are replaced (not mutated) so concurrent Recent() callers can't observe torn reads.
- AssSubtitleFile.Parse caps input at 100 MB to prevent OOM on malformed sidecars.
- Wizard i18n guard relaxed to Math.min so partial locale translations override index-by-index instead of falling back entirely to English.
- Retention slider in Settings now runs to 365 days (matched the wizard, no more silent 90-day cap on save).
- Update banner no longer fires on 0.0.0.0 dev builds.
- AnalyticsEnabled default flipped to false to match every "off by default" string in the UI.
- Task-active count derived from FIX_TYPES.length (previously hardcoded "of 15", now correct for all 18 fix types).
- Obsolete ScheduledFixTime config field removed.

Bug-fix bundle over 0.9.9.3.

Duplicate detector no longer flags different files with a shared prefix as duplicates. Replaced the trailing-tag whitelist (which kept missing new suffix combos users reported) with file-name-based edition detection: any variation in the filename between two TMDb-matched files yields a different edition key when 'Treat editions as duplicates' is off. Covers 100% of possible suffix combinations. Byte-identical copies with the same filename still group as duplicates. Regression: 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Connecting the Dots.mkv' vs 'StarWarsCloneWars2003 - Bridging the Saga.mkv' â€” now stays as two separate entries.

Jellyfin sidecar files/folders are skipped by the Duplicate scanner before grouping â€” no more 'theme.mp3 in show1/ is a duplicate of theme.mp3 in show2/' reports. Covers theme/themevideo/poster/backdrop/logo/etc plus extras subfolders (extras, trailers, behind the scenes, deleted scenes, featurettes, ...) and per-item extras suffixes in both compact and spaced form ('-behindthescenes' and '- Behind the scenes'). Reference: https://jellyfin.org/docs/general/server/media/movies/#extras

Dismiss button on issue cards renamed to 'Ignore this' â€” the existing behaviour already blocks that file from re-reporting, the old label was just confusing.

New: notification badges on Issues (open count, cyan), History (failed rows count, amber), and Errors tabs (unchanged).

Version scheme: feature.feature.feature.bugfix â€” fourth digit increments for hotfixes.

New Overview banner warns when a MediaDash re-encode gets undone by something external (typically Sonarr/Radarr redownloading a "too-small" file whose size dropped below the quality profile minimum, but also fires on manual recycle-bin restores or backup-restore overwrites).

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. If the current file is within 10% of the original size â€” i.e. the same rough size we shrank down â€” the shrunk copy has been replaced. Only paths meeting that concrete size-match trigger the warning. False positives are limited to genuine restores, which are also worth surfacing.

The red banner shows the filename, the shrunk-to size, the current size, and the fix date. Dismissable per browser session; reappears on the next scan if the condition still holds.

Detection is evidence-based, not guessed: at the end of every scan MediaDash walks the last 30 days of successful non-dry-run history entries, and for each one where the ORIGINAL is still preserved in the recycle bin, compares the file currently at the same path against the recycled original. versions.changelog: Consider artist id when syncing favourites
Fix for tracks without album artist metadata.
Fixed audiobooks being incorrectly treated as music and sent to Last.fm as now playing tracks, scrobbles, or favourite updates.

Scrobble log messages now include the exact data sent to Last.fm, url encoded and without the credentials, so a rejected scrobble can be replayed as is. This also covers the album artist and the MusicBrainz id, which were never logged before, and makes characters that are invisible in a log, such as non breaking spaces in artist names, easy to spot. This only changes logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Playback events received from Jellyfin are now logged, in both the default and the alternative mode, to help debug reports of tracks that never get scrobbled. Some clients do not tell the server that a track was played or stopped, and until now there was no way to tell that apart from the plugin discarding the event. The reason a track was skipped is logged as well. This only adds logging, scrobbling behaviour is unchanged.

Scrobbles that Last.fm silently drops are now logged as warnings with the reason, instead of being reported as successful. Last.fm answers those with a normal HTTP 200 and no error code, so they were previously indistinguishable from accepted scrobbles in the logs. This does not change which scrobbles are accepted, it only makes the rejected ones visible.

This version requires Jellyfin 10.11.9 or newer. Jellyfin 10.11.9 changed an internal API the plugin relies on. Fixes the 'Import Last.fm Loved Tracks' task. Also refactored the settings page to use plugin-specific element IDs, avoiding clashes with other plugins' configuration pages - this might fix the user dropdown showing up empty for some users.

New API key and secret, since the previous one was blocked or deleted by the original project owner. After upgrading, every user will need to re-enter their credentials for the plugin to work again. There's no way to migrate the old credentials since the API key is different and we don't store the actual user password (we just use it to create a session key). This is a necessary change to keep the plugin working, since the stored session keys were generated with the previous API key that is not valid anymore.

name: Marquee Companion [✓✓]
description:
Adds four independent capabilities: server-side filtering by media-stream characteristics that Jellyfin's core API can't express (video dynamic range, codecs, audio channel count, and spatial audio), plus opt-in global recent-podcast discovery via Podcast Index using administrator-provided credentials, plus opt-in passwordless sign-in by emailed magic link over administrator-configured SMTP, plus an opt-in scheduled task that recovers the release date of items that arrived without one by reading it from the file name. The filtering API exposes a paginated, BaseItemDto-compatible endpoint and a capability endpoint for client feature-detection.

  plugin id, and behavior unchanged).

  parentId still returns the global value set.

versions.changelog:
## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.7.0.0
### New
- Jellyfin 12 support. Every release now ships two builds, one for Jellyfin 12 and one for Jellyfin 10.11, and Jellyfin installs the right one for your server automatically.
- Jellyfin 10.11.0 and newer are supported again. The previous release required at least 10.11.6.
- New "Disable rate limiting" option for self-hosted LRCLIB servers. It removes the delay between requests, which speeds up large libraries. Requests to the public lrclib.net stay rate limited.
### Fixes
- Tracks that only have an album artist tag (compilations, classical music, many rips) now get lyrics. Strict search used to give up without an artist tag, and fuzzy search ignored the album artist entirely.
- Fuzzy search now tries every artist tagged on a track instead of only the first one.
- A system clock jump (NTP correction, VM resume) can no longer stall lyric requests.

## v1.6.6.0
### Fixes
- The lyrics task no longer re-downloads tracks that already have synced lyrics on disk. When a track's lyrics were saved but the database still reported them as plain (Jellyfin doesn't refresh metadata after a download until the next library scan), the task kept "upgrading" the same tracks on every run. It now trusts the synced .lrc file already on disk and skips it. -> #43

## v1.6.5.0
### Fixes
- Build against Jellyfin 10.11.6 instead of always the latest release. Previous builds were linked against 10.11.10 assemblies, which made Jellyfin report the plugin as "not supported" (TypeLoadException) on older 10.11.x servers. The plugin is now compatible with Jellyfin 10.11.6 and newer. -> #55

## v1.6.4.0
### Fixes
- Lyric file detection now also checks Jellyfin's internal metadata folder, not just the media folder. With "Save lyrics into media folders" disabled, already-downloaded lyrics are detected instead of being re-downloaded on every task run, which also reduces load on lrclib.net -> #54

## v1.6.3.0
### What's New
- Optional self-hosted LRCLIB server URL: point the plugin at your own LRCLIB instance instead of lrclib.net. Subpath URLs are preserved and the URL is validated on save. Thanks to @Nausi-llon (#50).
- Built-in rate limiting for lrclib.net requests: enforces a 200 ms minimum gap between calls and honors HTTP 429 `Retry-After` so transient spikes back off cleanly instead of surfacing as per-track errors.
- Identifiable User-Agent on every lrclib request (`jellyfin-plugin-lyrics/<version> (+repo-url)`) so the LRCLIB operators can distinguish this plugin from `jellyfin/jellyfin-plugin-lrclib` (#49).

### Notes
- No configuration changes required for existing users — the self-host URL defaults to `https://lrclib.net` and the rate limit only kicks in under load.

## v1.6.2.0
### What's New
- Auto-removes the official "LrcLib Lyrics" plugin (`jellyfin-plugin-lrclib`) on startup if installed, since both plugins register the same lyrics provider and conflict. This plugin is a fork that fixes critical issues — see README. The old plugin can be reinstalled later to switch back.

## v1.6.1.0
### What's New
- Lyrics alternative discovery: skip re-downloading lyrics that already failed in a previous run
- Synced-lyric upgrade now checks the existing sidecar file before replacing plain text

### Fixes
- Stop matching instrumental tracks against unrelated songs: honor LRCLIB's instrumental flag, validate every match against requested duration and artist, and drop the track-name-only fuzzy fallback when artist info is available (#40)
- Scheduled task log: split DB-desync skips from "already synced" skips so plain `.txt` sidecars are no longer counted as synced

### Settings
- New configurable duration-tolerance filter (default on, ±15s) with UI toggle to tune or disable

### Notes
- Jellyfin 10.11.6 or newer is now recommended (see README)

## v1.6.0.0
### What's New
- Added song title cleanup to strip YouTube-style suffixes (Official Music Video, etc.) and duplicate artist names
- Added progressive search fallback: retries with fewer parameters when no results are found
- Added multi-artist support: splits "artist1/artist2" and tries each artist individually
- Replace non-synced lyrics with synced ones when available
- Sped up scheduled lyrics task

### Fixes
- Fixed DI issue with RetryStateStore causing plugin to malfunction on startup
- Fixed fuzzy search failing when album name is missing
- Fixed crash on missing artist or invalid id

### Defaults Changed
- Strict search is now disabled by default
- "Exclude album name" is now enabled by default

## v1.5.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.4.0.0
### What's New
- Added support for Jellyfin 10.11

## v1.3.0.0
### What's New
- Fixed a lot of plugin loading issues
- Fixed GitHub Action Workflows

### Technical Improvements
- Consistent versioning across all project files
- Better package compatibility with Jellyfin 10.9.x series
- Improved documentation and installation instructions

versions.changelog: Add an opt-in Jellyfin metadata source for YouTube IDs. Preserve filename and custom-regex matching as the default, read validated Youtube provider IDs imported from NFO uniqueid metadata, and expose the source choice in plugin settings.

Add Jellyfin 12 support. Retarget to .NET 10 and Jellyfin Controller 12.0.0-rc3, implement the new media-segment cleanup contract, and preserve the event-driven SponsorBlock workflow without enabling the core library segment scan.
Serialize SponsorBlock processing to avoid concurrent refresh and playback work for the same item. Bump the plugin version for local installation.

Add Done state with convergence-based polling. Videos older than 30 days (by YouTube publish date) are fetched once and frozen. Videos younger than 30 days are polled daily until segment data is unchanged for 5 consecutive checks, then frozen. Stale segments are now deleted when SponsorBlock data disappears. Daily scan task refactored to a clean two-phase dispatcher.

Add dedicated SponsorBlock log file (log_SponsorBlock_YYYYMMDD.log) in Jellyfin's log directory. All info/warning/error events now write to both the main server log and the dedicated file, so the plugin appears as a separate log entry in the Jellyfin dashboard.

Add comprehensive logging to the orchestrator and triggers. Every decision point (scope check, path empty, ID extraction failure, state-machine skip, segment write, state transition) now logs at information or debug level, so issues are diagnosable directly from the Jellyfin log dashboard.
Fix EnumerateScoped to discover Episode and Movie items, not just standalone Video. YouTube libraries imported as TV Shows store items as Episode type, which BaseItemKind.Video did not match.

Fix automatic loading for old archives and restore DLL-only release packaging. The daily refresh now discovers selected-library videos older than the sanity-check window, old untracked items use their Jellyfin DateCreated for the 48-hour decision, and NoData rows recheck after cooldown instead of being terminal.

Add a one-shot Force Scan button for existing archives. Admins can backfill every video in the selected libraries once, while the normal daily refresh stays limited to tracked Pending and HasData items. Includes duplicate-scan protection and status endpoints.

Repair pruned SponsorBlock segments on playback. When Jellyfin refreshes a changed media file it can delete generated MediaSegment rows while the plugin state still says HasData; playback start now verifies that Jellyfin still has segment rows and re-fetches/recreates them if they were pruned.

Fix delayed SponsorBlock loading. Register the daily refresh scheduled task so Pending items are retried automatically, correct the 24-hour playback retry condition, and wait for playback-start processing so freshly fetched segments can reach the first playback session.

Actually fix segments not reaching clients. Jellyfin's IMediaSegmentManager.CreateSegmentAsync expects the second arg to be the MD5-derived provider id (new Guid(MD5(name.ToLowerInvariant() UTF-16 LE)).ToString("N")), not the literal provider name. We were passing "SponsorBlock" verbatim, so stored segments didn't match any registered provider and the public MediaSegments API filtered them out. Pre-compute the hash and pass that. After upgrading, hit Reset on the config page so old segments get re-fetched under the correct provider id.

Fix segments not reaching clients. v1.1.0.0 dropped the IMediaSegmentProvider registration to avoid the slow scan, but Jellyfin filters segments by registered provider, so stored segments were never served. Re-register a stub provider (Supports => false, GetMediaSegments => empty) so Jellyfin recognizes 'SponsorBlock' as a known provider while the orchestrator stays in charge of fetching.

Add admin Reset button on the plugin config page that wipes SponsorBlock state and owned segments for items in the configured library scope, so the orchestrator re-fetches on next playback. Useful for re-fetching items whose SponsorBlock data became available after the initial scan.

Replace media-segment scan with event-driven orchestrator. Add daily refresh task at configurable hour. Add per-library scoping (empty by default — admin must opt in). SQLite per-item state machine (Pending/HasData/NoData) with 48h sanity check.
Remove non-functional user segment actions table from config page.
Initial release.

name: ShareLinks [✓✓]
description:
Adds secure, expiring guest-share links for Jellyfin items using temporary hidden users, one-use token redemption, restrictive policies, and scheduled cleanup.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 12:08 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/Franciskid/jellyfin-plugin-sharelinks
overview: Temporary guest links for Jellyfin movies and episodes.

versions.changelog: Fixes share links on Jellyfin 12 and the ShareLink button missing on new Docker installs.

Fixes redemption on Jellyfin 10.11.9 and later (#19). Jellyfin changed the signature of the method the plugin uses to set a guest's password, so every link failed with a MissingMethodException and the guest landed on the dead-link page. The plugin now picks whichever version of that method the server has, so the same build works on every 10.11 release. Tested on 10.11.8 and 10.11.11.

Guests are now blocked from other plugins' API endpoints on the server, not just hidden from their UI in the browser. A share guest holds a real Jellyfin token, so anything that only hid a button left the endpoint answering it. Jellyfin's own API is untouched: the share tag already limits it to the shared title, and playback needs it. The config page lists your installed plugins with a checkbox each, so you can let one through when it genuinely needs to serve guests, such as an intro skipper. The guest hidden selectors setting is renamed to say what it is: cosmetic, it tidies the view and enforces nothing. Also fixes the dashboard devices page coming up empty after a share expired: deleting a guest left its device row behind, and a device whose user is missing makes Jellyfin fail the whole device listing rather than skip one row.

Fixes a season share exposing the rest of the series: the tag was going onto the season's parent series, and Jellyfin treats a parent's tags as belonging to all of its children, so every other season became visible to the guest. Tagging now only ever goes downwards. Take this update if you have shared a season with a link that is still live. Also in this release: a link can be made multi-use from the create popup so several people can use it until it expires, with a configurable ceiling on how many watch at once (ten by default), and the dashboard gains a "Clean up finished links" button that removes revoked, expired and failed records.

The ShareLink button now sits in its own section at the bottom of the item menu, and only appears for a movie, series, season or episode instead of turning up on things like a cast member. It is properly admin only again: the current user was cached for the whole page, so switching accounts in the same tab could leave the button visible to a normal user (the server always refused them). Share tags are hidden from everyone except admins, on the title and in the tag filter. Security: one-use links can no longer be redeemed twice, the configured maximum expiry is respected, the raw token is dropped from storage when a link dies, the token secret file is 0600, guest accounts can no longer sign in from the login page at all, and the runtime reflection shims around Jellyfin's APIs are gone.

Series and seasons can now be shared, not just single movies and episodes: the share tags the whole tree so the guest can browse and play everything inside it, and cleanup strips it all again. Expired or invalid links now show a friendly page that redirects to the Jellyfin home instead of raw JSON. The guest hidden selectors setting now defaults to empty.

ShareLink button on the item menu, temporary guest users confined by tag policy, expiring links with a date/time picker, admin dashboard with revoke, and a configurable guest lockdown that hides tag/genre/studio/cast links, the add-to-playlist and add-to-collection actions, and other plugins' UI. The creation popup is localized in English and French. Guest sessions are now minted server side: no password is ever stored or sent anywhere, the guest page only carries a session token, and expired guests are cleaned up every 30 minutes.

name: Native Trickplay [✓✓]
description:
Generates HLS I-frame variants so Apple TV / AVPlayer clients get native
scrubbing thumbnails on the transport bar — no client-side overlay needed.
One-time ffmpeg cost per item, then cached.
Includes a configurable daily prune scheduled task (orphan removal,

Universal Repo:  
Generated: 12:08 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/HarshLabs/jellyfin-plugin-native-trickplay
overview: Native HLS trickplay for AVPlayer-based clients (Apple TV).

versions.changelog: Videos whose HEVC stream declares a level above 5.0 (common with certain x265 encodes) were rejected by the Apple TV when served through the trickplay-enabled playlist, and the player fell back to the thumbnail track. The playlist now also offers a level 5.0 entry, the same approach Jellyfin uses for its own playlists, so these videos play normally with scrubbing thumbnails intact. No change for other videos.

- Fixed: trickplay playlists and image segments now enforce each user's library access and parental controls. Previously, any signed-in user could request the scrubbing thumbnails of items outside their allowed libraries.
- Improved: the dashboard's item list loads dramatically faster on large libraries (it no longer reads every cached playlist from disk just to show cache status).
- Improved: changing "Concurrent encodes" now takes effect immediately — no server restart needed.
- Fixed: corrupt video files could make HDR detection time out, producing washed-out thumbnails for HDR content.
- Fixed: searching with an extremely large season or episode number could error the item list.
- Hardened the release pipeline: build steps are now pinned to exact, immutable versions.

After updating, restart your server once as usual. No cache regeneration is required.

If you reinstall Jellyfin (or its database gets rebuilt) and point the plugin back at your existing cache folder, the plugin now relinks every cached entry to your library automatically — no re-encoding, no lost cache.

- New: orphaned cache entries (from a reinstall or database rebuild) are automatically relinked to your items at server startup and before every scheduled prune run.
- New: the dashboard shows a warning banner with a one-click "Relink orphaned entries" button whenever orphaned entries are detected.
- Fixed: Cache Status no longer counts orphaned entries as cached (previously it could show 100% coverage while every item listed as "not cached" and playback re-encoded).
- Fixed: the daily prune task no longer deletes a reinstalled server's still-valid cache — it relinks first and only removes entries that truly match nothing.

Update, restart your server once, and your cache reconnects on its own within about 30 seconds — or press the new Relink button on the plugin dashboard.

Fixes playback stalling on Apple TV when audio is passed through unchanged (stream copy). The playlist could advertise the wrong audio format, which made the player wait forever for audio it was never going to get. If playback ever froze right after turning subtitles off, this is that fix.
Fixed playback breaking on SDR variable-bitrate files when trickplay is enabled. Affected videos could freeze mid-playback or get stuck on a loading screen when resumed; they now play normally.

* On HDR sources, tone mapping now runs on the GPU when your ffmpeg build supports it (OpenCL for Intel QSV / VAAPI / AMD on Linux, CUDA for NVIDIA, Metal on macOS). The previous CPU tone-mapping path was the dominant cost on HDR content — moving it to the GPU is the bulk of the speedup. Falls back to the old CPU path automatically when no GPU tone-mapping filter is available.

* The ffmpeg filter chain now thins frames down to the trickplay rate (one every couple of seconds) before any per-frame work runs. Previously every decoded frame was transferred GPU → CPU before being discarded — for a 2-hour 4K HDR source that's hundreds of thousands of wasted full-resolution transfers.

* New "GPU tone-mapping for HDR" toggle in the plugin settings, on by default. Disable it if GPU tone-mapping misbehaves on your hardware — encodes still benefit from the filter-chain reorder.

* Encodes that hit a GPU tone-mapping issue now fall back to CPU tone-mapping automatically (keeping hardware decode), and only drop to full software decode if the hardware decoder itself fails. The dashboard's hardware-path column shows what's actually in use (e.g. "QSV+OCL", "VideoToolbox+VT") so you can see the path each encode is taking.

A user on an Intel iGPU reported that a 2-hour 4K HDR film took ~90 minutes to generate on the prior version. The same encode finishes in roughly 10 minutes on this version.

Previously, if you deleted a library from Jellyfin, the plugin's
"Find & select items" list and the daily pre-generation task kept
seeing items from the removed library until Jellyfin's next library
scan cleaned them up — which meant inflated totals on the dashboard
and the nightly task wasting time encoding files that were no longer
in any library.

The plugin now scopes its lookups to the libraries currently visible
in Jellyfin, so the moment you remove a library the dashboard total
matches the Cache Status widget and the pre-gen task stops touching
those items.

No action required — just update the plugin and the next dashboard
load will reflect the correct counts.

Avoids advertising an iframe trickplay variant whose playlist resolves
to a valid-but-empty stub on cache miss — that combination can stall
AVPlayer on tvOS 26 with seek-shifted on-demand transcodes. Trickplay
appears on the next playback session once the warmup task generates
the cache.

* Search results above 200 items now load progressively. Default page is 500; 'Load more' appends the next batch and 'Load all' pulls everything matching the current filter.
* New 'Select all N items matching this filter' link appears once you've checked some visible items in a paginated result. Click it to select every match — including items not yet rendered. The bulk Generate or Evict action then operates on the entire match set, not just the page in front of you.
* Selection persists across pagination — checking an item on page 1 stays checked when you load page 2.
* 'Clear selection' link in the banner dismisses an all-matching selection. Filter, sort, or search changes also reset selection automatically.

Cancel active encodings

* New "Cancel" button on each in-flight row in the Encoding-in-progress panel, plus a "Cancel all" button in the footer.
* Works for both queued items (waiting for an encoder slot) and items currently being encoded.
* Existing cached trickplay for the canceled item is preserved — only the in-progress attempt is dropped.
* Cancel is idempotent — a second click is harmless.

Release notes now reflect actual changes per release. Prior versions all showed "Initial release" due to a publishing oversight.

name: Mind the Gaps [✓✓]
description:
Scans your library for gaps (missing movies in partially-owned collections and franchises, missing series content, unowned titles from actor and director filmographies, and related recommendations) using TMDB, Trakt, TheTVDB, and TVmaze, with music and book sources (MusicBrainz, OpenLibrary, Discogs), and reads the watchlists and want-lists you already keep on those sites. Presents an easy todo list for filling out your collection, diagnoses why a title is reported missing, surfaces where to watch each item, and can optionally mint native virtual placeholders for missing items.

versions.changelog: 10.11.11.0 - Want to watch gains three options, all off by default and all requiring the arrived-titles playlist (contributed by David Rappo, @rappo, in PR 21): the home row can lead with the titles already on your playlist, a title comes off the playlist once it is watched (a series once every episode is played), and a movie or series page gets a bookmark button among its own. Plugin rows are reachable with a TV remote's D-pad. Not interested, off by default, lets each user hide a title from their own Web UI pages without hiding it for anyone else. A user with a parental rating limit sees the Web UI sections narrowed to the titles that limit allows, rather than none of them. The home Discover row, the Want to watch row, and the item page rows each have a placement setting; existing settings carry over. The Gaps Report's toolbar is grouped by what each control acts on, every header has a select-all, a line above the list says how many rows the filters hide, and Add to TODO is now Add to watchlist. The report is usable at phone width, and the settings page has collapsible sections, a search, and better screen reader support. A new scheduled task, Prune gaps from deleted items, takes deleted library items out of the report: a gap they were the only source of is removed, and one with other sources moves to the next. It has no default schedule; it waits for a running scan, and a second scan waits for the first. Recommendation groups link to the owned title they came from. Books get an OpenLibrary id field and albums and artists a Discogs id field in the metadata editor, with a link on the item's page; a dedicated OpenLibrary or Discogs plugin takes over when installed. Links are built from each title's ids when the report loads, so a link plugin installed later applies everywhere. The report takes far less memory and disk (on a library with 83,000 gaps, about 1.6 GB down to 200 MB in memory and 245 MB down to 131 MB on disk), loads in about half the time, and is written far less often during scans and where-to-watch lookups. Existing reports convert on first load; a report saved by this version cannot be read by an earlier one, so going back shows an empty report until its next scan.

10.11.10.0 - The Maintenance section has a Fulfillment queue for an administrator who fetches titles by hand. It folds every user's TODO list into one row per title, sorted by how many people still want it, names who is still waiting, and shows the streaming-service icons as soon as the queue opens, with the same links a TODO row already has. Mark fetched closes the title for every requester in one action, and Verify all checks the queue against the library and closes a title you already have, however it arrived. With Everyone's watchlist on (off by default), that same household list is a Discover source and leads the Discover view of every domain it has entries for. Send to the acquisition stack is done from the Gaps Report. The report's Send action has a quality profile picker, filled from the stack's own profile list and preselecting the profile you configured, so an older title the default profile cannot find a release for can still be sent. The report's My TODO list popup is gone; the Fulfillment queue is where an administrator sees every list. The report's multi-select bar can Acquire, Request, or Resolve a checked batch (Resolve applies one shared note), alongside Mint and Add to TODO. An administrator can manage another user's want-to-watch list. With "Want to watch: move arrived titles into a playlist" on, a title that is in the library moves into that user's own Jellyfin playlist the next time it is verified, so it shows up in every client. The playlist is named Want to Watch unless you change it, and only a real file counts as arrived. Amazon and web-search links for a book or album include the author or artist, on the report, the Web UI, and the Fulfillment queue. TMDB lists, Trakt lists, and OpenLibrary subjects are set with the same chip pickers the other curated sources use. A book's dialog loads its description from OpenLibrary when you open it. Studio pages, off by default, add a Missing from the studio row of that studio's movies you do not own, on the list page you open from a movie's studio credit. A library that sets a metadata fetcher order keeps TVmaze in the series check. TVmaze is not a Jellyfin metadata fetcher, so it is always asked and ranked last.

Gaps now show real cover art for books (bibliography and subject lists), music (MusicBrainz discography and artist works), and series completion episodes (TMDB, TheTVDB, and TVmaze all supply a still where they have one) instead of a blank thumbnail, falling back to the placeholder rather than a broken-image icon when a cover fails to load; MDBList entries carry a poster and description like every other source. A creator's page can be trimmed further with a minimum TMDB vote count for a movie credit and a minimum episode count for a TV credit. The TODO list shows an image and release date per entry. Sending a whole-series gap to Sonarr from a filmography, recommendation, or favorites entry sends the series' own title rather than the name of whatever surfaced it, and a rejected Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr request shows the service's validation message instead of a raw response body.

10.11.6.0 - The lists you already keep elsewhere now feed the report, and anything you have since filled in clears off it. Switch on any of the personal lists in the settings and each arrives as its own group on Discover: your IMDb watchlist or any public IMDb list, your Trakt watchlist, your JustWatch watchlist, your MDBList watchlist, your Discogs wantlist, your OpenLibrary "Want to Read", your favorite series on TheTVDB, and your TMDB watchlist and favorites once you connect your TMDB account, which is two clicks with nothing calling back, so your server needs no public address. An IMDb list of people is read as a filmography to fill in instead, which is what lets you follow a director or an actor you own nothing by yet. Discover groups all of it under proper headings, the lists you keep first, then the lists you pointed the plugin at, then what your own library suggested; a list that was read and holds nothing you are missing says so rather than not appearing at all, and one that could not be read says that instead. Anything you have acquired can be cleared without a rescan: a refresh control on every row and every heading checks your library right now and drops what you hold, "Clear what I have" does the whole filtered tab at once, and an acquired title leaves every tab it appeared on, so one film clears out of its collection, the studio set that wanted it, its director's filmography, and any list that suggested it. Whatever survives that can be re-checked against its providers in the background, which also picks up what has been added to a collection, discography, or bibliography since the last scan. The TODO list checks the same way, and both Markdown exports check before writing, so an exported list is what you still need rather than what the last scan believed. Titles with no release date at all are treated as not yet out, badged Announced and hidden under "Hide upcoming", with music and books exempt because a sparse entry for an old release often carries no date. Diagnose no longer reports a mix-up over an announced title that shares its name with something you own: the one on your shelf is an earlier, different release and nothing needs fixing. Scanning and clearing also read far less of your library than they did, so a long scan no longer holds it in memory while it waits on the providers. A Trakt list stopped at its first 100 items and an MDBList list at 1000; both now read to the end. An acquisition URL carrying a username and password is redacted before it reaches the log, and every other configured secret travels in a header that is never logged.

10.11.5.0 - Fixes installing on a server running an earlier 10.11 patch. The plugin declares the 10.11.0.0 ABI but was built against the 10.11.11 assemblies, which stamp their own patch number, so the package asked any server for 10.11.11 and a server on an earlier patch refused to load it. It is now built against 10.11.0 and loads on any 10.11.x server. The identification audit reports series whose episodes are split across two folders that map to the same season, listing each folder and its episode count so you can see which one to keep. The gaps report and the settings are separate dashboard pages now: the report opens without the settings form attached, the plugin's Settings button opens the settings, and resetting the scan rotation and removing minted items move to a Maintenance section on the report, beside the library they act on. Shared report links and exported audit dossiers still open the report. In the TODO list, the source column says what it is showing, using the same wording as the report's section buttons (the series for an episode, Discover for a recommendation, the creator, the set), instead of a bare name that read as a wrong series when you added a whole show, and a movie or show with no JustWatch link of its own gets a JustWatch search, in the list and in the Markdown export.

10.11.4.0 - Discovery lists: complete or explore a curated TMDB list, MDBList community list, or Trakt list the way you complete a collection (a TMDB list takes a pasted themoviedb.org/list URL, a Trakt list a numeric id or slug), complete a Books subject from OpenLibrary, and try any source from a Run button without a full scan. Series completeness now follows your library's own providers, merging TheMovieDb, TheTVDB, and TVmaze season by season in your order and reconciling episodes by air date and folded title, so a renumbered or merged two-part episode reads as owned; the per-provider checkboxes are gone, and you can re-check one series without a rescan. Music and books are on by default, Creator works surfaces an owned person's missing series as well as films, and Discogs completes a label's releases and an owned artist's discography quickly and accurately. Diagnose and the identification audit cover albums and books, explain an episode-numbering mismatch, and export an AI-analysis dossier. Round out a gap with a personal TODO list, a send to Radarr, Sonarr, or Jellyseerr, or a reversible virtual placeholder for any domain. The report regroups its settings, labels every tab for the media type in view, enlarges titles, collapses sections, and keeps shareable links short, while scans shrug off a transient provider failure and never log an API key.

10.11.3.0 - A new Discogs source completes curated record labels and an owned artist's discography (needs a Discogs token), chosen with the same type-ahead chip picker as studios and keywords. Diagnose goes deeper and wider: a networked "Deeper analysis" compares external ids to tell a real misidentification from a coincidental title clash, episode and season gaps get their own diagnosis that spots a same-named reboot mis-tagged onto a series (the V 1984 versus V 2009 case), and album and book gaps are diagnosable too. The report now links out everywhere: music rows link to MusicBrainz and Discogs, books to OpenLibrary, the Diagnose ids are clickable, and each creator or set group header links the source itself (an author's OpenLibrary page, an actor or director's TMDB page, an artist's MusicBrainz or Discogs page, a studio, keyword, label, or collection page); every link carries a per-provider CSS class, a data-provider attribute, and a title and aria-label, so a theme can inject service icons (the README has a ready-to-paste snippet under Advanced CSS customization). Under the hood, every external call now sits behind a read-through cache with proactive per-service rate pacing (MusicBrainz and Discogs) and a circuit breaker that moves the scan past a down service, the scan runs its sources concurrently and streams results into the report per item so a slow provider no longer holds up the others, and stable id-to-name lookups are cached for far longer. The library no longer reports a reboot's later seasons as missing episodes of the single-season original, a Name-plus- year match now prefers an exact-year hit over the one-year tolerance, and the Books (OpenLibrary) source is hardened against real-world author data. In settings, the Discogs toggle and token sit in the Data sources section, and Markdown exports are named by domain so different tabs no longer overwrite each other.

10.11.2.0 - The first public release since 10.11.1.0, rolling up the 10.11.1.x betas. The headline is Diagnose: a per-gap popup explains why something is reported missing, laying the gap and the owned items that look like it side by side and leading with a plain verdict (owned under the wrong id, an owned item already holds this id, stale, a wrong kind of id, or genuinely missing); a "Deeper analysis" button confirms against the source provider, and a library-wide identification audit runs the same check and downloads as Markdown. Diagnosis weighs both title and year, so a remake that shares a name with something you own (the 1960 Ocean's Eleven against the 2001 remake) is no longer reported as that title under the wrong id. Curated studio and keyword sets are now chosen with a type-ahead chip picker (search TheMovieDb, pick a match, it becomes a removable chip), keyboard and screen-reader accessible, and the Set completion tab groups by kind of set (collections and franchises, studios, keywords, series, and discographies). The Markdown exports gained structure: grouped sections, a table of contents, and native collapsible blocks (closed by default) for a large export. Also: a JustWatch search button on rows that lack a JustWatch link; titles that begin with "The" file under both T and the next word's letter; provider overviews are stripped of stray HTML and episode and season rows gained their search and open icons; a fresh install opens to settings until the first scan; and the settings panel warns about unsaved changes. Breaking change: the old free-text studio-names field was removed in favor of the chip picker, so any studios configured by name (rather than id) are dropped and must be re-picked.

10.11.1.0 - Initial release. Mind the Gaps scans your library and builds a dashboard todo list of what is missing or worth adding: movies missing from a collection or franchise; missing seasons and episodes (optionally cross-checked against TVmaze and TheTVDB); films from an owned actor or director's filmography (with an independent Trakt cross-check); curated studio and keyword sets; and TMDB recommendations. Experimental music and books sources are included too. It shows where to watch each gap, links out to TMDB, IMDb, TheTVDB, and JustWatch, and can optionally mint reversible virtual placeholders for missing collection movies.

name: Subtitle OCR [✓✓]
description:
Converts embedded image-based subtitle tracks (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to external SRT or ASS files using nOCR pattern matching. Pure managed code: no Tesseract and no native libraries, using the ffmpeg your server already ships. The .nocr database format is interchange-compatible with Subtitle Edit, so databases trained or corrected in its GUI drop straight in. A scheduled task scans your Movie and Episode libraries and writes a subtitle file beside each image-based track. OCR text is optionally spell-checked with Hunspell and corrected with Subtitle Edit's OCR fix lists, both fetched on demand.  
  
Universal Repo:  
Generated: 12:08 UTC  
Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr/main/manifest.json  
Github: https://github.com/IDisposable/jellyfin-plugin-subtitleocr
overview: OCR image-based DVD and Blu-ray subtitles to SRT or ASS

versions.changelog:
Recognition is far more accurate and roughly three times faster. The bundled Latin database carries glyph shapes trained on real disc fonts, so few characters read as the unknown box. A file gives up every subtitle track in one pass rather than one pass per track, tracks recognize in parallel (Max parallelism leaves half the cores to playback), and image buffers are reused, so a run no longer drives the full garbage collections that interrupt playback. The matcher takes the best matching glyph rather than the first the database lists, reads case from the image's own x-height and cap height, splits a merged glyph pair, matches a multi-segment glyph on shape at any size, and follows the line's italic state so a stray mid-word italic reads as the run around it. Whether a track is light text on a dark outline or the reverse is read off the track itself, per track, so the Invert luma setting is gone, and word spacing is calibrated to real disc fonts.
Output keeps more of the disc. ASS carries the color the subtitles were drawn in as its style, with an override only on the lines that differ, places an off-center sign on the full alignment grid, escapes a literal brace, and rounds its timecodes; Auto picks ASS for a track that is positioned or uses more than one color. A cue never ends after the next one begins, a too-short cue is held to a 750 ms readable minimum, and a re-sent duplicate cue merges with its neighbor.
Text correction covers misread digits (a 1 between letters as l or I, a 0 as o), the two-letter words It, Is, In and If, a lowercase l after a speaker label, split contractions and quotes, punctuation spacing, a leading speaker dash, curly quotes, and padded sound-cue brackets. An accented Latin letter foreign to the track's language folds to its base ("Nothing" for "Nothińg"), keeping each language's own accents and leaving cast and character names alone. Spell-check protects names in singular and plural and runs before sentence casing, so a misread at the start of a line resolves against the dictionary instead of freezing into a name. The l-to-I fixes are English-only, so French keeps its elided articles. Language and hearing-impaired detection read a cue's words, not its markup, so close languages like Danish and Norwegian separate, and a track the database cannot really read is discarded rather than shipped.
The extraction log is its own dashboard page, with a Reprocess all button that runs the reprocess task and shows its progress, and a per-row reprocess for a single item. New settings: Fold foreign accents (on), and Aggressive OCR fixes (off) for the riskier digit twins 5/S and 8/B on a poorly scanned disc. The plugin is built against 10.11.0, the target ABI it declares, so it loads on every 10.11 server.

Output format is now selectable: SRT, ASS, or Auto, which decides per track and writes ASS only when a cue sits away from the bottom of the screen (PGS carries the position), so an ordinary track keeps the universally supported format. OCR text is spell-checked with Hunspell, protecting Title-case proper nouns and words drawn from the item's Jellyfin metadata (title, overview, series, cast and character names) so show and character names survive. Subtitle Edit OCR fix replace lists are applied when present; dictionaries and fix lists download on demand and re-download once older than a configurable age. A track with an undetermined language now has one detected from its OCR text and is named accordingly, and the track title, forced, hearing-impaired, and commentary flags appear in the file name so commentary tracks are identifiable. A hearing-impaired track is recognized from its own text when the source flags nothing, which is the norm for a remuxed disc. New OCR corrections cover misread apostrophes in contractions, mid-word capital X, V, and I, optional ellipsis folding, and bogus italic runs around single characters and punctuation. An unread glyph now costs nothing when matching a word against the dictionary, so "batt□e" resolves to "battle" and a damaged name can be restored from the item's metadata. A new "Reprocess extracted subtitles" task re-OCRs every logged file from its source with the current settings. Each file is probed with a single ffprobe pass rather than two, and only one OCR or reprocess task runs at a time.

Detect image-based subtitles by probing every Movie and Episode with ffprobe, since Jellyfin does not store PGS/VobSub streams in its metadata. A per-file cache skips files that are unchanged and were probed within a configurable window, with a force-rescan option. Word spacing now scales with subtitle line height, fixing spaces inserted between every letter on HD Blu-ray text. New options: extract only selected languages, discard a track whose dropped-event ratio is too high (removing any stale SRT), and a filename tag ({name}.{lang}.OCR.srt, shown as the subtitle title) so the plugin only ever overwrites or deletes its own output. A config-page modal lists every extracted file with a link to its movie or episode. The scheduled task now sits under its own category.

Initial production release. OCRs embedded image-based subtitles (VobSub/DVD and PGS/Blu-ray) to SRT files using nOCR pattern matching, with Subtitle Edit-compatible .nocr databases. Pure managed code: no Tesseract, no native dependencies. Optionally skips image tracks whose language already has a text subtitle.

versions.changelog: # 🚀 A New Foundation for File Transformation File Transformation **3.0.0.0** is a major overhaul of how the plugin integrates with Jellyfin. The transformation system has been rebuilt around standard ASP.NET Core middleware, removing much of the version-specific runtime patching that File Transformation previously relied on. Alongside **Jellyfin 12 support**, this release drops support for **Jellyfin 10.10.7** and lays a much more maintainable foundation for future Jellyfin releases. > ## 🙌 Huge thanks to @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv > > A massive part of this release is thanks to **@4eh5xitv6787h645ebv**, who took on the major overhaul of File Transformation's core architecture in PR #58. > > The move away from the old Harmony/MonoMod-based interception system to standard ASP.NET Core middleware is a significant piece of work. It not only makes File Transformation substantially easier to maintain, but also resolves an entire class of compatibility problems that caused the plugin to malfunction or be disabled on certain Jellyfin versions and platforms (#20, #35, #62, #64, #70, #71). > > This is far more than a small patch or isolated feature - it fundamentally improves the foundation the plugin is built on. A huge thank you for the time and effort that went into it. ## ✨ New Features * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and the newer Jellyfin server architecture (#34). * Replaced the previous Harmony/MonoMod-based web interception system with standard ASP.NET Core `IStartupFilter` middleware (PR #58, @4eh5xitv6787h645ebv). * Added support for unregistering transformations through `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing dependent plugins to cleanly remove transformations when required. * Added support for synthesising virtual files for registered transformation paths, restoring support for plugins such as Plugin Pages where the underlying file doesn't physically exist. * Added ETag generation and `304 Not Modified` support for transformed content. * Added Brotli and gzip recompression of transformed responses for remote clients. * Added automatic MIME type detection for virtual transformed files. ## 🛠️ Improvements * Removed platform-specific DLL extraction and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * Removed dependencies on Harmony, MonoMod and Prometheus from the core transformation pipeline. * Improved compatibility across Jellyfin versions and platforms by moving the transformation system onto standard ASP.NET Core APIs (#20, #35, #62, #64). * Added per-transformation error isolation so a failure in one plugin's transformation won't prevent other transformations from running. * Made transformation registration, removal and execution thread-safe. * Added regex caching and timeout protection for transformation matching. * Improved handling of `Accept-Encoding`, including proper quality-value (`q`) parsing. * Improved LAN detection for IPv6-mapped IPv4 addresses. * Improved proxy caching behaviour by correctly setting `Vary: Accept-Encoding`. * Reworked HTTP handling to use a shared `HttpClient` with appropriate timeouts. * Hardened named-pipe transformations with timeouts, size limits, EOF handling and improved resource cleanup. ## 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). 🪲 Bug Fixes * Fixed a class of failures where Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching could cause File Transformation to malfunction or be automatically disabled on startup (#20, #35, #62, #64, #71). * Fixed #70 where transformations could attempt to use a disposed `IServiceProvider` after Jellyfin restarted, resulting in `500` responses across the web UI. * Fixed transformed content potentially retaining stale trailing bytes when a transformation produced a shorter result than the original response. * Fixed failures in one transformation potentially breaking the entire transformation pipeline. * Fixed potential `HttpClient` resource leaks. * Fixed named-pipe transformations being able to hang indefinitely or loop on zero-byte reads. * Fixed incorrect handling of disabled compression encodings such as `gzip;q=0`. * Fixed failed virtual-file transformations returning an empty successful response instead of reverting to the original `404`. * Improved middleware failure handling so the original response is served if transformation or recompression fails. ## 💻 Developer Compatibility The existing `PluginInterface.RegisterTransformation` API and registration payload remain compatible with previous releases, so plugins using a standard transformation callback **should not need to change how they register transformations**. There are, however, some changes to transformation execution that plugin developers should be aware of: * Added `PluginInterface.RemoveTransformation(Guid)`, allowing plugins to explicitly unregister a previously registered transformation. * Assembly callbacks still receive the same payload and are expected to return the transformed content as a `string`. * Invalid or failed assembly callbacks now **fail safely rather than falling through to another configured callback mechanism**. Plugins should ensure their callback assembly, class and method names are valid. * HTTP transformation callbacks must now return a **successful HTTP status code**. Non-success responses are treated as a failed transformation rather than using the response body as transformed content. * HTTP callbacks now have a **15 second timeout**. * Named-pipe callbacks now have connection/error handling and a **50 MB maximum response size**. * Failed transformations now leave the original response untouched rather than potentially replacing it with invalid or partial output. These changes are intended to make transformations significantly safer and more predictable, but plugins relying on the previous fallback or error behaviour should review their integrations when updating. ## ⚠️ Compatibility * **Jellyfin 10.10.7 is no longer supported.** * Added support for **Jellyfin 12** and its newer server architecture (#34). * Users remaining on Jellyfin 10.10.7 will need to stay on an earlier File Transformation release until they upgrade Jellyfin. * Removed legacy Harmony/MonoMod runtime patching and version-specific Jellyfin shims. * File Transformation now relies on standard ASP.NET Core middleware rather than patching Jellyfin internals, providing a much more stable base for future Jellyfin versions. ## Contributors * 4eh5xitv6787h645ebv ## ❤️ Support If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27). Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.
